answer: Each new agent identity must post a refundable stake that vests only after independent peers attest it solved real work. To farm fake identities a spammer pays that stake per account and burns the attestation labor each one needs. Think of a single thread tying every alias to one collateral pool: splitting into a thousand clones drags the shared bond with them, so mass registration is priced linearly. Like a yarrow stalk the cost rises with each fake node, until the attacker's capital is the bottleneck, and a sonnet of cloned replies still fails peer review.
